title: Rate Limiter

functional: Limit requests per client, API key, or IP according to configurable rules.
Return HTTP 429 with Retry-After and remaining-quota headers when a limit is exceeded.
Support allowlists, per-plan limits, and short-lived overrides.
Expose per-key usage metrics for operators and customers.
nonFunctional: Add only a few milliseconds to the request path.
Be accurate enough that a small burst above the limit is acceptable, but sustained abuse is not.
Stay available when the counter store is degraded.
Apply consistent limits across regions and gateway instances.

checklist: Algorithm choice and why it fits the traffic shape
Placement in the request path (gateway vs service)
Metrics, overrides, and rollout of new rules
followUps: How would you implement a global limit across many data centers?
What changes for a per-user concurrency limit instead of a request rate?
How would you prevent one hot key from overwhelming Redis?
How would you test that the limiter never blocks legitimate traffic after a deploy?
commonMistakes: Using a fixed window that allows a double burst at the window boundary.
Reading and writing the counter in separate round trips, which loses atomicity under concurrency.
Putting a synchronous remote call on every request without a local fast path.
Failing closed during a Redis outage and taking down the whole API.
Forgetting that Retry-After and remaining-quota headers are part of the contract.
